title: Seller Moment Mapping Cookbook (wip)
content:
Context:
This is a deliberately compact, modular set of seller-facing snippets and a micro-deck architecture for fast pilot qualification and runbook handoffs. Goal is to give SEs and sellers 30–120 second rehearsable "speaking moments" (playlets) + a short set of lightweight artifacts to attach to outreach: a 30s value line, 90s technical summary, 2-slide fallback graph, and a one-paragraph CFO econ nugget.

Why a cookbook:
- Field asks for bite-sized, persona-specific lines that are A/B testable in customer conversations.
- Many existing battlecards are long; sellers need executable micro-plays that map to real moments (pilot kickoff, capacity objection, latency SLA ask, procurement).
- We want to standardize quick canary/fallback language so SEs and ops are consistent when handing off to engineering or closing traps.

Structure of this doc:
1) Moment mapping grid (short)
2) Persona micro-scripts (30s / 90s)
3) Technical fallback graph (two-slide narrative)
4) Quick pilot checklist to attach to demo/poc emails
5) Experiment ideas + metrics to capture
6) Open Qs / TODOs

1) Moment mapping (3 columns = moment, friction, seller action)
- Pilot kickoff: Align on success metrics, initial throughput targets. Seller action: Say "We'll start the pilot with a 24–72 hour load profile and a latency SLO you name — we'll instrument tokens and cost per 1k so we can snapshot economics after first 2k requests."
- Integration architect eval: Concerned about API parity and SDKs. Seller action: 90s tech summary + repo link + small integration sample (node/python).
- Capacity objection (cost): concerned about bill volatility. Seller action: show Dedicated reserved example + quick math (expected tokens * 50% batching win = adjusted cost).
- Compliance/procurement: wants data residency and logging. Seller action: outline Private deployment options (VPC + KMS) and two-page security brief.
- Outage/fallback concern during demo: worried about model flakiness. Seller action: give fallback plan: 1) lower-capacity but compatible model, 2) automatic region spill, 3) API-level retry.

2) Persona micro-scripts
A) Integration Architect — 30s pitch:
"We expose the same inference API you know (REST + SDK) and we provide model variants you can pin per-route. For a quick test we can wire a proof-of-concept in two endpoints: 1) hosted sandbox for dev and 2) a pinned dedicated runner for performance tests. I can share a 10-line Node example right now."

90s extension (if they ask about ops):
- how we route requests (policy-based),
- KV / prefix caching that preserves latency while reducing tokens,
- how we handle sequence length variability (auto-kernel selection and batching).

B) Platform Engineer — 30s pitch:
"We provide reserved pools and autoscaling policies with SLO-backed latencies. If you need hard isolation, we have a private deploy option. For the pilot, we'll instrument token-level latency breakdowns and a per-route error budget."

C) CFO / Finance — 30s pitch:
"We can run a 30-day pilot and show per-monthized cost projection after we profile your workload. Two levers move the needle: batching and quantization profile. We estimate 30–60% effective token-cost savings on typical UI chat workloads after optimization."

Objection handling quick bullets (friction -> line):
- "We already have vendor X": "We position Redwood as a serving layer — same models, easier to operate and cheaper per token at scale because of caching and continuous batching."
- "Latency is critical": "We can pin a model on Dedicated pools and show 95th percentile numbers within 2–3 hours of a smoke test."

3) Two-slide fallback graph (narrative to use as image alt-text)
Slide A (one-line): "Graceful degradation keeps user flows alive"
Bullets: default route -> regional fallback -> cheaper-compatible model -> cached response.
Slide B (one-line): "Who takes the call (ops play)"
Bullets: seller identifies symptom -> SE toggles canary -> system falls back automatically -> ops notified + EMR (post-mortem) kickoff.

4) Pilot checklist (attach to pilot kickoff email)
- Goals: clear measurable outcome (e.g., reduce avg response time from X to Y, or achieve cost-per-1000 token below $Z)
- Data to share from customer: sample prompts, sequence length histogram, expected QPS
- Our deliverables: sandbox endpoint, 2 integration snippets, telemetry dashboard link, cost snapshot after 2k calls
- Roles: Seller (pilot lead), SE (technical lead), Infra (on-call), CS (success manager)
- Acceptance criteria: 3 business flows exercised, error rate < 1% within SLO window, and handoff doc produced.

5) Experiments to run (quick, measurable)
- Batching delta test: baseline vs. 2 batching profiles; measure tokens/sec and p95 latency.
- Quantization A/B: float32 baseline vs. int8-int4 profile; measure quality regression rate by eval set.
- Fallback vs. no-fallback: turn fallback on for 24 hours during load spike to quantify kept-conversions.
Metrics to capture: tokens per response, avg tokens per interaction, cost per 1k tokens, p95 latency, error rate per route, fallback invocation rate.

6) Slackable one-liners (copy/paste)
- To ops: "Starting pilot: sandbox + dedicated pin; will ramp QPS to 8/min for 48h, tagging with pilot:ACCT1234"
- To legal: "Pilot will use hosted sandbox data; we can move to VPC if required — attaching security brief."

Open questions / TODOs (working list)
- Define standard template for "pilot acceptance criteria" (owner: Maya)
- Add a short code gist for Java + serverless embedding quickstart (owner: Jonas)
- Confirm which benchmarking graphs we can ship as PNGs for email attachments (owner: Luis)

Appendix: example 90s technical summary (copy to SE notes)
"Redwood exposes REST and SDKs for sync and streaming. Our runtime performs continuous batching and KV caching, and selects optimized kernels based on sequence distribution. For pilots we recommend pinning a model variant on a dedicated pool to establish a latency baseline, then run 2 optimization experiments (batching profile and quantization) to hit cost targets while monitoring quality with a small eval set. We instrument token-level telemetry and provide per-route latency and cost breakdowns in the console so finance and platform teams can reconcile charges quickly."

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep this doc intentionally short — the field will prune what they don't use.
- Convert the two-slide fallback graph into a single PNG in the next pass.
- Run a playtest with 2 SEs next week; capture favorite micro-lines and update the 30s/90s bank.

Revision history:
- 2025-01-08: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2025-01-22: added persona lines and checklist (Jonas)
- 2025-02-22: added experiments + linked artifacts (Maya).

Quick contact: aisha@redwood-inference.com — ping for playtest scheduling or if you want a 15min dry run for wording.
